name: PMS7003 particulate matter (PM2.5) sensor
description: Plantower slim laser-scattering dust sensor reporting PM1.0, PM2.5 and PM10 mass concentration (µg/m³, 0-500 effective, >=1000 max, resolution 1) and particle counts per 0.1 L over a 9600-baud UART (3.3 V logic). The bare sensor needs 4.5-5.5 V for its fan and draws up to 100 mA; this adapter boosts a 3.3 V supply to 5 V for it. Sold as: Soldered PMS7003 sensor adapter (333058) with a PMS7003 plugged into its 1.27 mm 2x5 socket, 6-pin 2.54 mm header: VCC, GND, RX, TX, RESET, SET.
eli5: A thin box with a tiny fan pulls air past a laser and counts the dust and smoke specks, then tells your board how dirty the air is.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 3.3 V (3.0-5.5 V): an on-board TPS613222A boost converter makes the sensor's 5 V

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground (the sensor's metal case is grounded too)

pins.name: RX
pins.description: Sensor serial input (3.3 V logic): wire to the board's UART TX; only needed to send commands

pins.name: TX
pins.description: Sensor serial output (3.3 V logic, 9600 baud): wire to the board's UART RX

pins.name: RESET
pins.description: Reset, active low, pulled up inside the sensor; leave open if unused

pins.name: SET
pins.description: Sleep control, 3.3 V logic, pulled up inside: high/open = run, low = sleep

supplierQuery: PMS7003 particulate sensor with adapter board
buildNotes: Power the Soldered adapter's VCC from 3.3 V: its TPS613222A boost converter makes the 5 V the sensor's fan needs (allow about 180 mA from 3.3 V). The data pins are 3.3 V logic, safe straight into an ESP32 or Pico.
Cross the serial wires: adapter TX (sensor output) -> board RX, adapter RX (sensor input) -> board TX. RX is only needed to send commands.

9600 baud 8N1. In active mode (power-up default) the sensor sends a 32-byte frame on its own about every 2.3 s (200-800 ms when readings change fast): 0x42 0x4D, length 28, 13 big-endian words, then a 16-bit sum of the first 30 bytes. Resync on 0x42 0x4D and drop frames whose sum does not match.
Data 4-6 are PM1.0/PM2.5/PM10 'under atmospheric environment' (use these); data 1-3 are the CF=1 values meant for factory use.
Leave SET and RESET unconnected unless you use them (both are pulled up inside); SET low stops the fan. Readings need at least 30 s after waking to settle.
Mount it at least 20 cm above the floor, keep the inlet and outlet clear, and keep the grounded metal case away from other conductors.

example.code:
from machine import UART, Pin
from pms7003 import PMS7003

uart = UART({UART_ID}, baudrate=9600, tx=Pin({RX}), rx=Pin({TX}))
pms = PMS7003(uart)
while True:
    r = pms.read()
    print('PM1=%d PM2.5=%d PM10=%d' % (r['pm1_0'], r['pm2_5'], r['pm10']))

test.title: Reports the PM1.0, PM2.5 and PM10 set on the sliders

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading (4 difference(s) settled by a third reading with quoted evidence). Not yet tested on real hardware.
